explanation: The statement is about the library's own definitions. `power p n` is the n-fold convolution power of a function on a finite group, defined with `conv p q g = ∑ h, p h * q (h⁻¹ * g)`. The lemma says that if p is nonnegative and positive on every element of a list, then `power p l.length` is positive at `l.prod`. Its proof is an induction using the library's own `conv_pos_of`. I read the local definitions of `conv`, `power` and `conv_pos_of` in the same file. Mathlib has no analogue of this finite-group convolution power over ℝ-valued functions with a positivity-at-list-product statement. Mathlib's convolution (`MeasureTheory.convolution`, `Measure.conv`, `Finsupp`/`MonoidAlgebra` multiplication) is stated for different objects. I found no Mathlib declaration that carries this content.
